[#asio-yield-current]
== Yield measurements of the shipped implementation

This fresh local experiment began at `2026-11-07T04:21:58.914Z` using `HeadlessChrome/156.0.8078.4`. It measures the current shipped Asio backend with Release `-O3`, independently of the historical October experiment below. Both JavaScript and Wasm artifacts and the implementation source are fingerprinted before execution. Builds and conformance tests from this session completed before sampling; other user and OS activity is not controlled.

The interval is the handoff to the browser and return to {cpp}, excluding the callback batch. It includes the dispatcher return/reentry boundary. {cpp} and JavaScript monotonic clocks share the browser time origin; wall-clock bracket checks and pure-JavaScript controls test the measurement. The default remains `100` handlers per turn. This is a scheduling policy, not a time budget or a guarantee of rendering/input latency.

All 442 cases passed validation: 970,139,132 operations and 9,429,856 timestamp pairs. Seven primary repetitions and three secondary-control repetitions are retained. Percentiles in the table are medians of per-run percentiles, not a pooled tail guarantee. Dividing the measured gap by the turn limit is an amortized estimate; it does not measure the callback work itself.

Additional groups cover no exceptions, ordinary nonisolated pages, tracing, clocks, synchronous language crossings and arithmetic work. A zero clock tick does not prove zero cost. The complete distributions, ranges and paired controls remain in `runs.csv` and `summary.json`.

`bench/yield/results/2026-11-07` retains the generated results, build/environment metadata and raw evidence archive with its SHA-256 file. `bench/yield/README.adoc` gives the reproduction commands. This is a headless otherwise idle-page experiment, not a loaded application or remote CI run.
